text:
Scott Morrow scored his first goal as a Ranger on Nov 16 against Montreal, and then spent the next week as the subject of a debate. The Hockey Writers said he deserves to stay in the lineup, Yahoo Sports said he's earned a permanent spot, Sports Illustrated and The Hockey News wondered whether he would keep it once Sean Durzi returned.

The answer, at least for one game: Durzi came back against Carolina on Nov 22, and Morrow played 17:36 on the third pair beside Braden Schneider, his biggest workload of the season.

The numbers support keeping him. New York gets 56% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, a bit better than without him. He has two points in nine games. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 33% of his shots coming off the rush last season, nearly double a typical defenseman.

He was a second-round Carolina pick in 2021 out of UMass. What to watch: whether he keeps the spot as the Rangers' blue line gets healthy.
